# Intake Brief — Validate all card text (CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0)

## Problem statement

The integer-economy migration (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) scaled coin/reputation
**data** ×100 but only partially updated the **card text**. Business,
community-space, upgrade, and staff `description` fields were scaled, but every
event `effect` field was left at its pre-migration display-scale value (e.g.
`evt-festival` reads `+2 coins` while its `coinDelta` is `200`), and
`evt-shopping-spree` still shows a fractional `+2.5 coins` (data `250`).
Players therefore read card text that disagrees with the amount the engine
actually applies, with the activity log, and with the raw-integer HUD. The
same stale values also remain in every other player-visible surface that
repeats card coin/reputation amounts — card-face SVGs, tooltips, tutorial copy,
staff-skill descriptions, and the `docs/main-street/*` reference material.

## Users

- **Player** — needs each card's text to state the same coin/reputation amount
  that will actually be applied, so purchase/play decisions are informed.
- **Game designer / balancer** — needs `card-data.csv` text and data columns to
  agree so balancing is based on accurate descriptions.
- **Developer / QA** — needs a durable check that catches future card-text/data
  drift instead of relying on manual review.

### User stories

- As a player, when I read an event card's effect text I see the same
  coin/reputation amount that the game applies and that the activity log shows.
- As a designer, I can trust that every card description matches its
  `card-data.csv` values without mental ×100 conversion.
- As a developer, a failing check tells me exactly which card's text no longer
  matches its data.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Every player-visible card-text surface is ×100-consistent with card
   data.** Every numeric coin/reputation mention in card text equals the
   corresponding data column (`coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`,
   `reputationPerTurn`, `ongoingCost`, `reputationBonus`, `incomeBonus`,
   staff-skill magnitudes) under the documented ×100 scale. The audited
   surfaces are: the `card-data.csv` `description` and `effect` columns;
   card-face SVG text (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and committed SVG
   artifacts); tooltips (`MainStreetFormatting.ts`); tutorial copy
   (`TutorialFlow.ts`, `i18n/tutorial-en.ts`); staff-skill descriptions
   (`MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`); and the `docs/main-street/*` reference
   material. All event `effect` texts are scaled (e.g. `evt-festival`
   `+2 coins` → `+200 coins`); `evt-shopping-spree` `+2.5 coins` →
   `+250 coins`. No fractional coin/reputation value remains in any
   player-visible card text.
2. **Non-coin/reputation numbers are unchanged.** Percentages (`45%`, `90%`,
   `120%`), durations (`3 turns`), hand-slot counts, levels, and the
   `{SYNERGY_RATE}` token are out of scope and verified unchanged.
3. **Automated regression test guards against drift.** An automated unit test
   parses every card's text coin/reputation mentions and asserts they match the
   card's data columns under the documented ×100 scale, failing with a message
   that identifies the offending card. The test must run in the `unit` profile
   and fail if a future edit desynchronises card text from card data.
4. **Tests and artifacts updated.** Existing test expectations that reference
   old text values are updated; committed card SVG artifacts are regenerated to
   match the corrected text; `npm run build` and the unit test profile pass.
5. **Documentation updated.** Every doc carrying stale fractional card values
   (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and the other `docs/main-street/*` files
   identified during implementation) is revised to the integer scale; code
   comments describing the old scale (e.g. the `{bonus}` example `+2 coins` in
   `TutorialFlow.ts`) are corrected. All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
   or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`.** Text is corrected to match data; data
  values are not changed to match text.
- **Only coin/reputation amounts scale.** Percentage, rate, duration, and count
  values are untouched; `{SYNERGY_RATE}` stays a rate token resolved at render
  time.
- **Cover every player-visible surface (producer-confirmed).** Card-face SVGs,
  tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions, and docs are all in scope,
  not just the CSV `description`/`effect` columns.
- **Automated tests required (producer-confirmed).** The regression guard is an
  automated unit test, not a manual checklist.
- **No rebalancing.** Apply text-only ×100 corrections; any balance change is a
  separate work item.
- **CHANGELOG.md excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `card-data.csv` business/community-space/upgrade/staff `description` fields
  were scaled ×100 by CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6.
- Every event `effect` field retains its pre-migration value (small integers),
  while `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` were scaled ×100 — e.g. `evt-festival`
  `effect: "+2 coins to all Culture businesses and +1 reputation."`,
  `coinDelta: 200`, `reputationDelta: 100`.
- `evt-shopping-spree` is the only card with a fractional value in text:
  `"+2.5 coins to all Commerce businesses."` (`coinDelta: 250`).
- The HUD renders raw integers (`Coins: 1000`); the activity log renders raw
  integers via `describeEventEffects` (`+200 coins`); SpecificSynergy event
  tooltips show only the (small) `effect` text, so the mismatch is visible to
  players.
- `TutorialFlow.ts` resolves `{bonus}` from `coinDelta` (`+${coinDelta} coins`
  → `+200 coins`) but its doc comment still says `e.g. '+2 coins'`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (and several other `docs/main-street/*`
  files, including `specialization-skills.md`, `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `the-build-gdd.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`,
  `content-design-and-progression.md`, and `prd-multi-use-card-economy.md`)
  still use fractional values such as `+0.4/turn` and `0.25 coins/turn`.
- No automated test currently compares card text amounts against card data;
  existing card tests (`event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`,
  `card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `card-schema-validation.test.ts`,
  `csv-checksum.test.ts`) use synthetic fixtures.

## Desired change

Audit every player-visible card-text source — CSV text, card-face SVGs,
tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions, and docs — scale all
coin/reputation amounts to match the integer data (×100), remove the last
fractional value, add an automated regression test so text/data drift is caught
automatically, and refresh stale docs and comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — scale every event `effect` coin/rep
  amount ×100 and fix the `evt-shopping-spree` fractional value; check remaining
  `description` fields.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — tooltip rendering of
  `effect`/`description`; confirm text/data consistency.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — card-face
  text; confirm integer rendering and regenerate committed SVG artifacts.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — staff-skill
  descriptions; verify already-scaled values.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — `{bonus}` doc comment and any
  tutorial card-value copy.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — tutorial copy referencing
  card coin/reputation values.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip coin/rep
  values and card detail lines.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — committed card-face SVG
  artifacts; regenerate after text corrections.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and the other `docs/main-street/*` files
  with stale fractions — update to the integer scale.
- `tests/main-street/**` — new automated card-text/data consistency test plus
  updated expectations.

## Related work

- **Potentially related docs**
  - `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — canonical card text/data source.
  - `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — card catalogue with stale fractional values.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — card tooltip text builder.
  - `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — card-face SVG text.
  - `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — `{bonus}` interpolation and stale comment.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — staff-skill descriptions.
- **Potentially related work items**
  - `Move to integer numbers for coins and reputation (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6)` —
    completed; the migration whose text updates this item validates.
  - `Dynamic synergy bonus text on business cards (difficulty-aware percentage, Option B) (CG-0MS9GS91E004OAF4)` —
    completed; dynamic card text rendering.
  - `Synergy bonus on business cards (CG-0MRXYHNHB006F0U9)` — completed;
    synergy text semantics.
  - `In main street log should show total effects (CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ)` —
    completed; log integer deltas that already disagree with event text.
  - `Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT)` —
    completed; tutorial copy review precedent.
  - `Fix card rendering, UI overlay, and formatting tests (CG-0MTKLQ1P40091YTH)` —
    completed; card rendering/formatting tests.
  - `Main Street Game over dialog is not showing text (CG-0MQ2IL40S0060FUG)` —
    completed; card/dialog text rendering precedent.
  - `Implement Multi-Use Card Economy in Main Street (CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7)` —
    completed; card-economy semantics behind the coin/rep values.
  - `Docs: tutorial-localization + README updates (CG-0MSLXJ1OK004LJKU)` —
    completed; tutorial/doc text-update precedent.

> **Automated related-work report:** `/skill:find-related` was run and inserted
> a report into the work item. Its findings are folded into the list above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: event `effect` scaling direction (confirmed ×100).** Producer
  confirmed event effect text scales ×100 to match `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`,
  consistent with the already-scaled business descriptions and the raw-integer
  HUD/log. The regression test encodes this.
- **Risk: natural-language parsing fragility.** Comparing text amounts to data
  columns requires parsing prose. Mitigation: constrain the test to well-formed
  `[+-]?N coins?` / `[+-]?N reputation` patterns and/or an explicit per-card
  expected-value map, with a clear failure message naming the card.
- **Risk: scope creep into rebalancing.** Mitigation: apply only ×100 text
  corrections; file a separate balance work item for any value change.
- **Risk: missed text sources.** Coin/reputation copy lives in CSV text, SVGs,
  tooltips, tutorial strings, staff skills, and docs. Mitigation: grep the repo
  for fractional coin/rep patterns and for the `effect`/`description` columns,
  and regenerate committed SVG artifacts.
- **Risk: expanded scope increases effort.** Producer confirmed "cover
  everything" and automated tests, which widens the surface beyond the CSV and
  raises the estimate. Mitigation: effort/risk re-estimated after the scope
  confirmation.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** scope covers every player-visible surface that
  repeats card coin/reputation amounts (CSV text, SVGs, tooltips, tutorial
  copy, staff skills, docs); percentages, durations, and counts are out of
  scope.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** the regression guard is an automated unit test.
- **Assumption:** documentation updates cover the docs carrying stale card
  coin/reputation values; unrelated doc drift is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

An initial brief was drafted from the seed context, then three clarifying
questions were put to the producer and answered (2026-09-24, interactive
reply). The brief has been updated to the confirmed answers.

- **Q: Should event `effect` text be scaled ×100 to match
  `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` (e.g. `+2 coins` → `+200 coins`)?** —
  **Answer (producer): yes.** Source: interactive reply; consistent with the
  already-scaled business descriptions and the raw-integer HUD/log. Research:
  `git show 192943c9` showed the migration scaled descriptions but not the
  event `effect` column; `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` and
  `MainStreetStateLog.ts` render raw integers.
- **Q: Is "all card text" limited to the `card-data.csv` `description`/`effect`
  columns, or should it cover tooltips/SVGs/tutorial copy/docs too?** —
  **Answer (producer): cover everything.** Source: interactive reply. The brief
  now scopes card-face SVGs, tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions,
  and `docs/main-street/*`.
- **Q: Is an automated regression test the expected way to "ensure" ongoing
  correctness, or is a one-time audit-and-fix sufficient?** —
  **Answer (producer): automated tests.** Source: interactive reply. AC3 is now
  a required automated unit test rather than a manual checklist.

**Research summary:** `wl show CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 --json` established the
migration contract (CSV ×100, integer-only UI). `git show 192943c9` confirmed
the migration scaled business/community/staff/upgrade descriptions but did not
touch the event `effect` column. A CSV parse of all 173 rows found exactly one
remaining fractional text value (`evt-shopping-spree`, `+2.5 coins` vs
`coinDelta=250`) and showed every event `effect` still at display scale
(e.g. `evt-festival` `+2 coins` vs `coinDelta=200`). `MainStreetFormatting.ts`,
`MainStreetStateLog.ts` (`describeEventEffects`), `MainStreetRendererHud.ts`,
`TutorialFlow.ts`, and `MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` were inspected to map the
text sources and confirm the HUD/log render raw integers. `docs/main-street/*`
was grepped and found to retain fractional values in `card-catalog.md` and
several other files. Existing tests (`event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`,
`card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `card-schema-validation.test.ts`,
`csv-checksum.test.ts`) use synthetic data and contain no card-text/data
consistency guard. The producer's three answers (×100 direction, cover
everything, automated tests) were applied to the problem statement, AC1/AC3/AC5,
constraints, and risks.

# Intake Brief: Check achievements after each action (not only at end of turn)

## Problem Statement

In Main Street, challenge ("achievement") completion is evaluated only during the end-of-turn **EndCheck** phase, so an action that satisfies a challenge produces no immediate feedback — the tracker, activity log, score bonus, and celebration all wait until the player ends the turn. This makes completed actions feel inert and delays reward feedback.

## Users

- **Main Street players** building a run and pursuing challenges.
- **AI / Monte Carlo / headless** consumers of the engine turn flow, which must behave consistently with the interactive path.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I place a card / make a purchase / perform any action that satisfies an active challenge, I want the challenge to register immediately (tracker, log, bonus, celebration) so the action feels rewarding.
- As a player, if I undo an action that completed a challenge, I want to be warned before the undo aborts/commits, so I don't accidentally lose or keep a completion unintentionally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After **any** action that satisfies an active challenge, the challenge is marked complete **immediately** (no end-of-turn wait): `activeChallenges[].completed = true`, the challenge ID is appended to `state.challengesCompleted`, and a `Challenge completed: <title> (+<pts> pts)` entry is added to `state.activityLog`.
2. Per-action evaluation applies to **all action paths**: the interactive command layer (`MainStreetCommands.ts`) and the engine `executeAction` path used by AI, Monte Carlo, and headless runs. The existing end-of-turn EndCheck evaluation is retained as a safety net for completions caused by the closing phases (Income / Incident).
3. In the interactive scene, the challenge **celebration VFX/SFX fires immediately** after the completing action (respecting reduced-motion), and the end-of-turn celebration does **not** re-fire for a challenge already celebrated mid-turn (no double-celebration).
4. Undoing the most recent action when that action completed a challenge shows a **confirmation warning dialog** that offers to proceed or abort. Choosing **Cancel aborts the undo entirely** (no state change); choosing to proceed **reverts the completion**: removes the challenge from `challengesCompleted`, clears its `completed` flag, removes the corresponding "Challenge completed" activity-log entry, and reverts the score bonus.
5. Redo re-applies the action and re-completes the challenge consistently (completion and celebration are restored on redo without duplicating log entries or celebrations).
6. Unit tests cover: per-action completion via the interactive command path; per-action completion via `executeAction`; no double-celebration at end of turn; undo-cancel leaves the completion and bonus intact; undo-confirm revokes completion, bonus, tracker state, and the activity-log entry; and that deterministic simulation (Monte Carlo / AI) outputs remain valid (or the baseline shift is measured and documented).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, help text, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular, correct any text stating challenges are evaluated only at EndCheck / end of turn (e.g. `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`).

## Constraints

- **Producer decision (Q1 = A):** completion is revoked on undo, but the player is given a warning that allows the undo to be aborted. Preserve "no revocation" outside of explicit undo.
- **Producer decision (Q2 = A):** per-action evaluation runs on all paths (interactive + `executeAction`/AI/Monte Carlo/headless).
- **Producer decision (Q3 = A):** immediate celebration after the action; end-of-turn celebration deduped.
- `state.activeChallenges` holds evaluator **functions**, so it must not be deep-cloned — the existing `captureSnapshot`/`safeClone` (`structuredClone` then JSON fallback) silently drops functions. The undo snapshot must capture challenge completion state in a cloneable form (e.g. `challengesCompleted: string[]` plus a per-challenge `completed: boolean[]` captured/restored by index) and never the full `activeChallenges` array.
- The undo snapshot currently captures `activityLog` but **not** challenge state; both must be restored atomically on undo to keep tracker, score, and log consistent.
- Reuse existing infrastructure: overlay dialog pattern (`createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, all overlay children parented into `hudContainer`, depth 199/200/201), celebration animator (`MainStreetAnimator.animateCelebration`), and audio (`SoundManager`, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, `SFX_KEYS.CELEBRATE = 'sfx-challenge-complete'`, `sfx-tf-mapping.ts`).
- Do not change the score formula (it already counts `challengesCompleted.length`); only the timing of completion changes.
- Deterministic simulation tests (Monte Carlo, AI win-rate) may shift because challenges now complete earlier; re-baseline or document the shift explicitly.

## Existing State

- `evaluateChallenges(activeChallenges, state)` is called only in `MainStreetEngine.ts` inside `processEndOfTurn` (`~L1606`) and `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` (`~L1946`), during **EndCheck**. This placement was intentional per CG-0MMJO6RUO1TH1O9V, which also established the "once complete, no revocation" rule.
- Interactive actions do **not** use `executeAction`; they dispatch through `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` (via `s.undoManager.execute(cmd)`) from `MainStreetTurnController.ts`. Only `community-favour` (interactive) and the AI/Monte-Carlo/headless paths call `executeAction`.
- `MarketActionSnapshot` (`MainStreetCommands.ts`) captures `activityLog`, `actionsRemaining`, `bankedActions`, etc., but not `challengesCompleted` or per-challenge `completed` flags.
- Celebration VFX/SFX is driven by `TurnResult.newlyCompletedChallenges` and triggered in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn` at end-of-turn.
- `performUndo` / `performRedo` already handle undo/redo UX (log entries, `animateUndoRedo`, refresh) and are the natural home for the warning dialog.

## Desired Change

- Evaluate challenges after every successful action.
- Surface newly completed challenges to the immediate caller so the scene can celebrate at once.
- Make challenge completion part of the undoable action state, with a warning-before-undo when a completion would be reverted.
- Ensure end-of-turn evaluation remains as a safety net without duplicating completions or celebrations.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — add a thin `evaluateChallengesAfterAction(state): string[]` wrapper (or reuse `evaluateChallenges` directly); keep the completion callback (log + `challengesCompleted`).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — call per-action evaluation after each successful action in `executeAction`; expose newly completed IDs to callers (richer return value or a transient state field); keep EndCheck evaluation as the closing-phase safety net; adjust `executeFullTurn` / `executeCompetitiveDay` so per-action and closing-phase completions are not double-reported.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — evaluate challenges inside each command's forward mutation; extend `MarketActionSnapshot` with `challengesCompleted` and per-challenge completion flags (cloneable form only); record which challenges a command completed so undo can warn about them.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — centralise command dispatch so each command's newly completed challenges are detected and celebrated immediately; implement the undo warning dialog + abort in `performUndo`; dedupe the end-of-turn celebration.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — expose/wire a shared command-execution helper if the centralisation lives on the scene.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — new `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog(challengeTitle, onUndo, onCancel)` following the `showSellConfirmation` / `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` pattern.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — reuse `animateCelebration`; add the undo-warning interaction if needed.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/*` — locale keys for the new dialog copy (follow existing i18n conventions).
- `tests/main-street/challenge-celebration.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts` — extend; add per-action and undo-revocation tests.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (and any help/tooltip copy) — update the "evaluated at end of turn / end of game" wording.

## Related work

- CG-0MMJO6RUO1TH1O9V — **EndCheck Evaluation & Scoring** (source of the current end-of-turn evaluation and the "no revocation" rule this item amends).
- CG-0MQS46G5U001CYUG — **Challenge celebration VFX and sound** (celebration animator/SFX infrastructure reused here).
- CG-0MMJO7COE009UG48 — **Challenge HUD Tracker** (tracker refresh path).
- CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ — **Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements** (blocked; terminology overlap).
- CG-0MU89K6UT007ZNKA / CG-0MU89K6AB001JQOW — **Document / wire deferred end-of-turn mutation** (may interact with undo and turn-flow sequencing).
- CG-0MTKLPTJP003HDA0 — **Fix activity log, challenges, and integration tests** (recent challenge/activity-log work).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Snapshot correctness:** challenge state must be captured/restored in a cloneable form; cloning `activeChallenges` would drop evaluator functions. Mitigation: capture `challengesCompleted` + completion flags by index.
- **Double-celebration / ordering:** immediate celebration vs end-of-turn celebration could overlap with action animations and the turn presentation sequence. Mitigation: dedupe via idempotent `completed` flags and only celebrate each completion once.
- **Simulation/balance drift:** completing challenges earlier can move score thresholds and end-condition timing in Monte Carlo/AI runs. Mitigation: re-run the Monte Carlo harness and AI win-rate tests; re-baseline or document.
- **Undo/redo atomicity:** restoring `challengesCompleted`, flags, and `activityLog` independently could desync. Mitigation: restore them together; add a test asserting tracker/score/log stay consistent after undo and redo.
- **Undo-warning interaction with animations:** `performUndo` early-returns while `uiPhase === 'animating'`; the dialog must integrate with that guard and not strand the scene in a blocked state. Mitigation: only present the dialog when an undo is otherwise legal, and restore `uiPhase` on both confirm and cancel.
- **Scope creep:** e.g. Steam-achievement sync, revoking completions on non-undo paths, or revamping the tracker. Mitigation: record as linked work items rather than expanding scope.
- **Assumption:** "achievements" in this item means in-game challenges (`activeChallenges` / `challengesCompleted`), not Steam achievements.
- **Assumption:** the warning dialog fires only when the command being undone actually completed a challenge this turn.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When an action completes a challenge and the player then undoes that action, what should happen?" — Answer (producer): **A — Revoke the completion, with a warning that allows the undo to be aborted.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Which action paths should evaluate challenges per action?" — Answer (producer): **A — All paths: interactive command layer and engine `executeAction` (AI, Monte Carlo, headless).** Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the celebration VFX/SFX fire immediately after the completing action?" — Answer (producer): **A — Immediate celebration after the action, with the end-of-turn celebration deduped.** Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143** – Rebalance card families across progression tiers (incl. tiering staff cards) (completed)
- **CG-0MLTSZI651HIVNM3** – Create GitHub Actions deploy workflow (completed)
- **CG-0MSN19DB4008TMPC** – Test contract: turn-limit end conditions (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: achievement, achievements, action, check, complete, currently, end, every, gives, rather, should, turn
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: action, check, checked, complete, currently, end, every, rather, should, turn
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — matched: achievement, achievements, action, complete, end, every, gives, rather, should, turn

## Goal

Write integration tests for undo/redo with challenge completions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Test: undo-cancel — player undoes an action that completed a challenge but cancels the undo via dialog; the challenge remains completed and score bonus intact.
2. Test: undo-confirm — player undoes an action that completed a challenge and confirms; the challenge completion is revoked (removed from challengesCompleted, completed flag cleared, activity log entry removed, score bonus reverted).
3. Test: redo after undo-confirm — redo re-applies the action and re-completes the challenge; no duplicate log entries or celebrations.
4. Test: redo after undo-cancel — redo is available (state unchanged) and re-applies the action with the same completion.
5. Test: no double-celebration — completing a challenge mid-turn and then ending the turn does not fire the end-of-turn celebration again.
6. Tests cover at least 2 different challenge types (one resource, one placement).

# Park should cost 40 coins (0.4) per turn to maintain

## Summary

Give the Main Street **Park** (`cs-park`) community-space card a per-turn running cost, so that placing a Park is no longer a free, costless synergy anchor. The producer directive reads "Park should cost 0.4 per turn to maintain"; because the economy is now integer-only (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6, ×100 rescale), the faithful value is **40 coins/turn**.

## Problem statement

The Park is the cheapest Tier-1 community space (cost 300) and currently has **no ongoing cost** (`ongoingCost` empty → 0). Playtest notes describe Park-spam ("Two Parks provide cheap Culture filler"; "The Culture-heavy cluster … generates massive synergy income") with no downside. The producer wants a maintenance cost so Parks impose a real per-turn drain and spamming them is a meaningful trade-off.

## Users

- **Player** — builds a Park-heavy Entertainment/Culture cluster and should feel the ongoing cash drain as a real strategic cost.
- **Producer / balance owner** — wants Park to stop being a free synergy anchor and to have a lever to curb Park spam.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I place a Park on the street I want to see that it costs me coins each turn, so I can weigh Park spam against my coin income.
- As a balance owner, I want the Park's running cost to appear in the card data, tooltip and card face so the cost is transparent and testable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-park` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` has `ongoingCost = 40` (the integer-economy equivalent of the specified 0.4/turn after the ×100 rescale, CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6).
2. **IncomePhase deduction** — at end of turn, each placed, **unsold** Park deducts 40 coins through the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path, alongside other community-space/staff/business costs, clamped at 0 coins and logged ("Community space costs: -N coins …") with an insufficient-funds log when the bank cannot cover it.
3. **Tooltip** — the Park community-space tooltip includes the ongoing-cost line `Ongoing cost: -40/turn` (auto-derived from `ongoingCost`); the Park description in `card-data.csv` states the running cost, matching the Library/Community Garden wording ("Costs 40 coins per turn to run.").
4. **Card face** — the street/market card overlay for a Park displays the 40 coin/turn cost in the two-tone cash line (the existing community-space overlay path, CG-0MTCP76MP0088TQW/CG-0MTDMOYOL008IQVO — no baked SVG change is expected since community-space ongoing cost was removed from the baked face).
5. **Sold-card exemption preserved** — a sold Park incurs no ongoing cost (existing CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA behaviour), verified by test.
6. **Tests** — existing Park assumptions are updated (`tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` "Park has no ongoing cost" and the mixed sold/unsold case; `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` "Park tooltip has no ongoing-cost line") and new/updated tests assert the 40/turn deduction, the tooltip line, clamping/insufficient-funds, and the sold-card exemption. Each test asserts a distinct behaviour (no redundant duplicates).
7. **Balance sanity** — the tutorial scenario (verified: it places no Park — its scripted market is Bakery/Laundromat/Festival) and the Monte Carlo balance guardrails remain green (or any drift is measured and reported in the work item); no guardrail band is silently widened.
8. **Docs** — `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (Park's `Ongoing/turn` column 0 → 40) and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (that table has no Ongoing column, so Park's row gains the "Costs 40 coins per turn to run." sentence, matching the Library row) are updated; any other doc that lists Park's ongoing cost (e.g. `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`) is checked and updated to 40 coins/turn; stale pre-rescale rows (e.g. `the-build-gdd.md` Park-as-business) are corrected or explicitly flagged.
9. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** coins/reputation are whole integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6). The literal value `0.4` rounds to `0` via `roundInt()` and is not a viable ongoing cost; it must be expressed as `40`. Do not reintroduce fractional coin values or per-card rounding.
- **Data is source of truth:** ongoing cost lives in `card-data.csv`; the tooltip, overlay and deduction all derive from it. No hard-coded Park cost elsewhere.
- **Charging semantics unchanged:** ongoing costs apply only to placed cards, exclude sold slots, and are clamped at 0 coins — Park must reuse the existing community-space mechanism, not a new one.
- **Balance values are producer-owned:** the 40 mapping is an agent interpretation, documented as an assumption; it should be easy for the producer to confirm or override.

## Existing state

- `cs-park` (`card-data.csv`): `cost 300`, `baseIncome 0`, `synergyTypes Entertainment`, `reputationPerTurn 0`, `ongoingCost` empty → `0`.
- Deduction engine: `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` sums each placed community-space `ongoingCost`, applies the Cost Cutter street reduction, rounds the **aggregate** via `roundInt()`, clamps the deduction at the coin bank, and logs the cost/shortfall; it skips `soldSlots`.
- Display: community-space tooltip in `MainStreetFormatting.ts` emits `Ongoing cost: -N/turn` only when `ongoingCost > 0`; the horizontal `+X / -Y` card-overlay cash line is built in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` and rendered by `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`. Community-space ongoing cost is deliberately **not** baked into the card SVG.
- Tests currently assert the opposite (`Park has no ongoing cost`, `Park tooltip has no ongoing-cost line`).
- Historical truth: the pre-×100 economy had Park `ongoing = empty`; Library `0.25`, Community Garden `0.1`, Health Kiosk `0.15`, Public Art `0.25`. Commit `192943c9` (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) scaled these ×100 to 25/10/15/25, so `0.4 → 40`.

## Desired change

1. Set `cs-park.ongoingCost = 40` in `card-data.csv` and add the running-cost sentence to Park's description.
2. Update the tests that encode "Park is free", add explicit 40/turn coverage, and verify the tooltip line and sold-card exemption.
3. Update the balance/design docs that list Park's ongoing cost.
4. Confirm the Park card overlay shows the 40/turn cost and that tutorials/balance guardrails are unaffected (or report measured drift).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — set `cs-park` `ongoingCost` to `40` and update the description text.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — update "Park has no ongoing cost" and the mixed sold/unsold Park case; add Park deduction + clamping + sold-exemption coverage.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` — replace "Park tooltip has no ongoing-cost line" with an assertion that the tooltip contains `Ongoing cost: -40/turn`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Park row gains the 40 coins/turn running-cost note (the community-space table has no Ongoing column) and a rationale note.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — community-space table Park ongoing 0 → 40.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — revise any Park-ongoing statement / examples.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — note Park's new running cost (community-space curve excludes `ongoingCost`).
- `docs/main-street/the-build-gdd.md` — Park row currently lists a stale no-cost entry (verify/update).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — expected **no change** (already generic over `ongoingCost > 0`); verify only.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` / `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — expected **no change** (generic cash line); verify Park shows `-40`.

## Related work

- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 — integer economy ×100 rescale (defines the 0.4 → 40 conversion).
- CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA — sold cards excluded from ongoing costs (Park must keep this behaviour).
- CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE — business ongoing-cost rebalance (precedent for the ongoing-cost mechanic and tooltip/overlay display).
- CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE — community-space ongoing-cost / Library repurposing (the mechanic Park will use; "Park model" synergy participation).
- CG-0MQBLGQ2Z0066UGP — "Park is not a business" reclassification (`cs-park` identity).
- CG-0MTR39XO6002CBB1 — open: "Events income/costs should be shown on the business cards" (card-cost display surface).
- Original source: ContextHub WL-0MTH6O957004963U (deleted; transferred here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (value):** "0.4" is in the pre-×100 scale, so the current-economy value is **40** coins/turn. Evidence: the requirement pre-dates commit `192943c9` (2026-09-02), which scaled every `ongoingCost` ×100, and the engine rounds to integers. **Producer should confirm 40.** If the producer instead wants a literal sub-1 cost, the integer economy must be revisited (out of scope here).
- **Balance drift risk:** Park is a Tier-1 card used by tutorials and Park-spam playtests; a 40/turn cost can shift tutorial economy and Monte Carlo guardrails. Mitigation: run the relevant tutorial/balance tests and report any drift rather than silently widening bands.
- **Correctness risk:** a naive change could double-charge or break the sold-slot exemption. Mitigation: rely on the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path and cover it with tests.
- **Doc drift risk:** Park's ongoing cost appears in several docs; missing one leaves stale guidance. Mitigation: grep all Park/ongoing references as part of the change.
- **Scope-creep risk:** re-tuning other community spaces (e.g. Playground or Fountain also have no cost) is a separate balance decision — capture any such opportunity as its own linked work item, not in this change.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The original ContextHub intake was blocked on producer questions. Those are now resolved from repository evidence (the item description notes agents on this project can resolve them directly):

- **Q (original): What project/domain does `park` belong to, and which codebase needs the change?**
  — **Answer (agent, from repo evidence):** Tableau-Card-Engine, Main Street game. The target is the `cs-park` community-space card. Source: ContextHub audit comment on WL-0MTH6O957004963U; `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`. Resolution of original Q1/Q2/Q5.

- **Q (original): What is a `park` and what is a `turn` in this context?**
  — **Answer (agent, from repo evidence):** `Park` is the Tier-1 Main Street community-space card `cs-park`; a `turn` is a Main Street turn whose end-of-turn IncomePhase deducts ongoing costs. Source: `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()`. Resolution of original Q2/Q3.

- **Q (original): What is the current behaviour and cost?**
  — **Answer (agent, from repo evidence):** Park has no ongoing cost (`ongoingCost` empty → 0); tests assert "Park has no ongoing cost" and "Park tooltip has no ongoing-cost line". Source: `card-data.csv`, `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts:179`, `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts:200`. Resolution of original Q4.

- **Q: What does "0.4 per turn" mean in the current integer economy?**
  — **Answer (agent, from repo evidence):** **40 coins/turn.** The directive pre-dates the ×100 integer-economy conversion (commit `192943c9`, 2026-09-02, CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6), which scaled every `ongoingCost` ×100 (Library `0.25 → 25`, Community Garden `0.1 → 10`, Health Kiosk `0.15 → 15`, Public Art `0.25 → 25`). `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` rounds the aggregate with `roundInt()`, so a literal `0.4` rounds to `0` and is not representable. Source: `git show 192943c9`, `git show 192943c9^:example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`, `MainStreetDifficulty.ts#roundInt`.

- **OPEN QUESTION (for producer confirmation, not blocking):** is 40 coins/turn the intended post-rescale value, or should Park's cost be a different integer? The agent proceeds with 40 as the documented interpretation; the producer may override this single value.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQQT9X45002WM4H** – Synergy only works for different businesses (completed)
- **CG-0MSBSC3PL002OA4G** – Unify currency formatting across card tooltips and card faces (completed)
- **CG-0MRCQL9KO007SUUJ** – Main Street income label: add Income: prefix, center on card, show in market (completed)

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtcp76mp0088tqw, 0mtdmoyol008iqvo, acceptance, add, agent (+301 more)

# Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (WL-0MTH6B20C002ZOM2) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

The Pawn Shop business card (`biz-pawnshop`, Main Street game, `Tableau-Card-Engine`) is currently **increasing** the player's reputation by +5 per turn and costs 300 coins to purchase — both incorrect per design intent. A pawn shop should be a low-reputation, budget-friendly establishment: it should **reduce** reputation by 0.1 per turn and be cheaper to acquire (200 coins at the ×100 scale, i.e. 2.00 in game terms).

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I expect placing a Pawn Shop on my street to slightly harm my reputation each turn (`-0.1`), not boost it, so that reputation decisions involve meaningful trade-offs.
- **As a player**, I expect the Pawn Shop to remain an accessible budget business (cheaper than the 300-coin tier-2 group) despite its per-turn reputation penalty.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect CSV card data and tests to stay internally consistent (numeric columns valid; ongoing-cost convention preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Negative reputation per turn.** `biz-pawnshop.reputationPerTurn` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` changes from `5` to `-10` (the ×100 integer-economy representation of the design value −0.1; see CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); placing the Pawn Shop on the street grid accrues a **negative** reputation delta (−10) during the income phase (`applyIncome`), never a positive one.
2. **Reduced purchase cost.** `biz-pawnshop.cost` in the CSV changes from `300` to `200`; the market purchase price for the Pawn Shop is 200 (2.00 at the ×100 display convention).
3. **Synergy opt-out unchanged.** The Pawn Shop still provides and receives **zero** synergy bonuses (`synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, no adjacency synergy) — unchanged behaviour (existing tests in `adjacency.test.ts` / `MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` still pass).
4. **Test coverage.** Add or extend automated tests asserting (a) the Pawn Shop's negative per-turn reputation and (b) its updated cost of 200; the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (card tooltips/descriptions generated from CSV, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` and any README/wikis as applicable, including code comments). Note: `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- CSV numeric columns are validated by `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`parseFloat`); `-0.1` is a valid numeric value.
- Costs use the ×100 integer convention (200 = 2.00 coins); `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw at income time (no ×100) — confirm via tests during implementation.
- **Do not** regenerate costs via the balance-cards curve tool (`src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts`): it would reassign tier bands. Its Pawn Shop special case (cost −2) applies only when `baseIncome === 0`, which is not our case — no algorithm change needed.
- Ongoing-cost convention (documented in `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts`) is `max(25, cost / 4)`. **Assumption (producer to confirm):** if `cost` becomes 200, `ongoingCost` follows the convention to 50 (currently 75). The producer's clarification specified only the purchase cost; do not change `ongoingCost` unless confirmed.

## Existing state

Current `biz-pawnshop` row in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`:

```
business,biz-pawnshop,Pawn Shop,300,230,Commerce,...,1,5,0,0,Trades second-hand goods. Does not provide or receive synergy bonuses.,2,...,75,...
```

- `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 230`, `reputationPerTurn = 5`, `synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, `tier = 2`, `ongoingCost = 75`.
- The Pawn Shop currently **adds** 5 reputation per turn (raw ledger units) and costs 3.00 coins (×100: 300).
- All six tier-2 businesses share `cost 300 / income 230 / rep 5 / ongoingCost 75`; changing only the Pawn Shop is a deliberate divergence.

## Desired change

| Field | Current | Desired |
|---|---|---|
| `reputationPerTurn` | `5` | `-10` (×100 integer economy; reduces reputation by 0.1/turn in design terms) |
| `cost` | `300` | `200` (2.00 at ×100) |
| `ongoingCost` | `75` | `50` — **assumption**, follows `cost/4` convention; pending confirmation |
| `synergyCoinBonus` / `synergyRepBonus` / `tier` / `baseIncome` | `0` / `0` / `2` / `230` | unchanged |

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ongoing-cost convention (assumption, unconfirmed).** Changing `cost` to 200 implies `ongoingCost = 50` per the documented `max(25, cost/4)` convention; the producer's clarification only covered the purchase cost. Implementer should confirm before touching `ongoingCost`; leaving it at 75 leaves a convention inconsistency (risk: low).
- **Unit conventions.** Costs are ×100 integers; `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw. If the game's ×100 scaling applies to reputation in the current branch, `-0.1` may need to be stored as `-10` — validate against the repo's existing tests before finalising the CSV value (risk: medium; mitigated by AC1's negative-delta assertion).
- **Do not regenerate balances.** Running the balance-cards tool would reassign the Pawn Shop's tier band and overwrite the manual cost; the change is a data-only edit plus tests.
- **Scope-creep guard.** The Pawn Shop's card *description* text could mention its reputation penalty, but that is an extra opportunity — record as a linked work item if desired, not part of this item's scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Pawn Shop row: `reputationPerTurn`, `cost` (and `ongoingCost` per assumption)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — template loading from CSV (read-only; verifies `-0.1` and `200` parse)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `applyIncome` reputation accrual loop (read-only; confirms negative deltas apply)
- `tests/main-street/…` — new/extended tests (e.g. alongside `business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` / `turn-cash-net.test.ts`) for negative rep/turn and cost 200
- `src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts` — no change expected (verify special case is unaffected)
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — update if the Pawn Shop row description changes

## Related work

- `WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02` — "End of game stats" (open; text-overlap match only, no dependency).
- `WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1`, `WL-0MT1KJNHE0048HW3` — text-overlap matches from the automated report; not related.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — documents the Pawn Shop no-synergy special case.
- Existing Pawn Shop synergy opt-out tests: `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/same-type-synergy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` (all covered by AC3).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

1. **Q:** "The description says 'Reduce the cost of the pawn shop to 2' — which field should be changed? `cost` (purchase price, currently 300) → reduce to 2? `ongoingCost` (per-turn operating cost, currently 75) → reduce to 2? Or some other cost field? The reputation change (from +5 to −0.1 per turn) is clear."
   **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "Neither should be reduced to 2. This is from when costs were lower, now it should be 200."
   **Final accepted answer:** the **`cost`** field changes `300 → 200` (×100 scale; 2.00 in game terms). The original "to 2" wording was from an earlier lower-cost economy and is superseded.
   Research summary: inspected `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (pawn shop row), `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (numeric validation), `MainStreetCards.ts` (template loading), `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (`applyIncome` reputation accrual), `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (ongoing-cost convention `max(25, cost/4)`), and `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`.

# Ensure every Main Street card has a dedicated 64×64 sprite

## Goal

As a player, every Main Street card shows distinct, recognisable art in its 64×64 left-art zone — no card falls back to the generic `Fallback` sprite in the market, hand, or street.

## Context

discovered-from:CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN

The 64×64 left-art redesign (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN, commit 38cf1f08) embeds a 64×64 sprite PNG into every card face and resolves it by card name via `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` (generated by `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`), falling back to the `Fallback` sprite when no dedicated sprite exists.

Today only 63 sprites exist for the 171 card templates in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`, so ~108 cards render the same generic `Fallback` art. The gaps:

- **Upgrade cards (39)** — names like `Upgrade to Patisserie`; many have a `targetBusiness` that does resolve to a sprite (e.g. `Diner`, `Hardware Store`, `Boutique`), so at minimum upgrades can inherit their target's art.
- **Staff cards (25)** — no sprites (`Assistant`, `Chef`, `Security Guard`, …).
- **Event cards (~44)** — no sprites (`Rainy Day`, `Block Party`, `Tax Audit`, …).

## Proposed approach

Decide the art strategy per family (to confirm during intake/plan):

1. **Upgrades** — derive art from `targetBusiness` (or an explicit override when `targetBusiness` is empty), so each upgrade shows the business it enhances.
2. **Staff** — add role/family sprites or a small set of shared staff art.
3. **Events** — add per-event sprites or a documented category mapping (e.g. incident vs opportunity, festival vs economic).

Then extend the resolver and/or art map accordingly, keeping `Fallback` only as a genuine last resort.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every card in `card-data.csv` resolves via `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite (any documented mapping/alias counts).
2. Upgrade cards resolve to a sprite derived from their `targetBusiness` (or a documented explicit override); no upgrade shows generic `Fallback` art.
3. Staff cards each resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card shows generic `Fallback` art.

## Goal

Parse and validate `games/manifest.json` and decide, per entry, whether the game is compatible with the launcher's core-engine version — as a pure, browser/Electron-agnostic module with unit tests.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). Realises AC1 (runtime game discovery metadata) and AC2 (core version compatibility check). Must not throw on malformed input — it returns a structured result so the launcher can degrade gracefully (AC4).

## Manifest schema (authoritative for this item)

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "games": [
    {
      "id": "golf",
      "sceneKey": "GolfScene",
      "title": "9-Card Golf",
      "description": "Lowest score wins.",
      "thumbnail": "assets/thumbnail.png",
      "coreEngineVersion": "^0.1.0",
      "entry": "entry.js"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Core version compatibility check** — Each game declares a `coreEngineVersion` (semver range) in its manifest; the launcher checks compatibility at load time and skips incompatible games with a clear error message in the Game Selector UI.
- **Core version compatibility check** — `parseGameManifest(json: string | unknown)` returns a discriminated result: `{ ok: true, manifest }` or `{ ok: false, errors: string[] }`; it never throws on malformed JSON or a wrong shape.
- Each entry is validated for required fields (`id`, `sceneKey`, `title`, `description`, `coreEngineVersion`, `entry`) with field-named error messages; duplicate `id` or `sceneKey` values are rejected.
- `splitByCompatibility(entries, engineVersion)` returns `{ compatible, incompatible }`, where each incompatible item carries a human-readable reason naming the required range and the launcher version.
- A `coreEngineVersion` semver range is honoured via the `semver` package (`semver.satisfies`); invalid ranges are reported as validation errors, not thrown.
- The launcher's engine version is exposed by the core engine (single source of truth) and consumed by the compatibility check.
- Unit tests cover every AC above, including missing manifest, malformed JSON, missing fields, duplicate ids, incompatible range, and invalid range.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/ui/game-manifest.ts`: types (`GameManifest`, `GameManifestEntry`), `parseGameManifest`, `splitByCompatibility`, `DEFAULT_ENGINE_VERSION`.
- Add `semver` (+ `@types/semver`) to `dependencies`.
- Export the engine version constant from `@core-engine` and reuse it.
- Tests in `tests/ui/game-manifest.test.ts` using the F1 fixtures.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/game-manifest.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `package.json`
- `tests/ui/game-manifest.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 loader test harness & fixture.

## Goal

Discover compatible runtime games from the manifest, dynamically import each game's ESM entry point in the renderer, extract its scene class and `GAME_INFO`, and return a merged, Phaser-ready catalogue — the heart of the plugin loader.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). Realises AC1 (dynamic scene discovery/registration) and AC4 (graceful degradation on a per-game load failure). Uses the F2 manifest parser and F1 fixtures; assets are resolved through F3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Runtime game discovery** — The Electron renderer reads a `games/manifest.json` from the content directory at startup, discovers each game's scene class, metadata (title, description, thumbnail), and registers it dynamically so it appears in the Game Selector alongside statically-registered games.
- **Runtime game discovery** — `loadGamePlugins(options)` is an async function accepting `{ contentDir, engineVersion, importer?, fetchManifest? }` with injected dependencies so it is unit-testable without Electron.
- For each compatible entry it dynamically imports the game's `entry` (resolved against `contentDir/games/<id>/`), obtains the exported scene class and `GAME_INFO`, and returns a `GameEntry` (with thumbnail resolved via `resolveGameAssetUrl`) plus the scene class to register.
- A failed import or a missing/invalid scene export is captured per game (id + reason) and does not prevent other games loading; the returned catalogue still contains the successful games.
- A missing or malformed manifest yields an empty dynamic catalogue plus a structured error — never a thrown exception.
- Returned scene keys are de-duplicated against the statically-registered catalogue (static wins; a conflicting dynamic game is reported as skipped).
- Unit tests cover: valid fixture load, mixed compatible/incompatible, malformed manifest, failed import, duplicate sceneKey, and injected-importer call counts.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/ui/GamePluginLoader.ts` exporting `loadGamePlugins` and result types (`LoadedGame`, `IncompatibleGame`, `PluginLoadError`).
- Resolve entry URLs with `new URL(entry, base)` and import via an injectable `importer` (defaults to dynamic `import()`).
- Tests in `tests/ui/game-plugin-loader.test.ts`.

- `tests/ui/game-plugin-loader.test.ts`

# Task: Create the nine `tce-*` GitHub repositories and push extracted history

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I can clone each per-game repository
(`tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`,
`tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`) plus
`tableau-card-engine-core` from GitHub with `--recurse-submodules`, then run
`npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`, and get a runnable
single-game TCE checkout — so the sibling-repo composition that F4/F9 built and
verified **locally** exists on the remote and is cloneable by anyone.

## Users (user stories)

- **Distribution maintainer** — creates the nine remotes **once**, in the final
  F9 Option C `src/` layout, so no history-rewriting re-push is ever needed.
- **Game developer** — `git clone --recurse-submodules
  git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git` and builds/tests the game against
  the engine pulled in as the `core` submodule.
- **Launcher / distribution builder** — composes a subset of the remote game
  repos as siblings (the `solo` and `full` presets) against fresh clones.

## Context

Split out of F4 (CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK) per operator decision: F4 delivers the
local per-game launcher scaffold (configs, `GAME_INFO`, build/test/package,
history-preserving extraction); creating and pushing the remote repositories is
a separate concern. The F4 producer gate deferred remote creation until the F9
Option C `src/` layout settled, so the nine repos are created **once, in the
final `src/` shape** — no history-rewriting re-push.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The nine repositories exist on GitHub under `TheWizardsCode` at the remotes
   recorded in `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`:
   `tableau-card-engine-core`, `tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`,
   `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`,
   `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`.
2. Each repository's default branch contains the extracted,
   history-preserving tree in the F9 `src/` layout (extraction via
   `scripts/extract-repos.sh`, scaffold via `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`):
   the core repo holds the engine + Gym + launcher shell and **no games**; each
   game repo has its source at repo-root `src/` and wires the engine as a
   `core` git submodule pointing at
   `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`.
3. From a **fresh remote clone**, `git clone --recurse-submodules <game-repo>`
   followed by `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm test -- --project unit`
   succeeds for at least **golf** and **main-street**.
4. The launcher can compose a subset of the **remote** repos as siblings (spot
   check: the `solo` and `full` presets build against fresh clones).
5. Evidence is recorded on this work item: the extraction commit count per repo
   (as F1 did) and the source monorepo commit SHA the nine repos were extracted
   from.
6. No CI pipeline and no npm publication are added (out of scope, per the epic
   constraints).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (In practice:
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 currently says the remotes are
   *not* created; `README.md`/`docs/DEVELOPER.md` clone guidance must document
   the `--recurse-submodules` workflow.)
8. Validation for the change: the extraction/scaffold unit suites
   (`tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts`,
   `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`) pass, and the published remotes
   are validated by the fresh-clone checks in AC3/AC4.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No CI pipeline and no npm publication (epic constraint).
- Never rewrite the source monorepo: extraction always operates on a clone
  (`git clone --no-local`); the monorepo `main` is never pushed to directly.
- `git filter-repo` is required and is **not currently installed** on this host
  (`pip install git-filter-repo` per
  `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`).
- GitHub org write access is required; the authenticated account
  (`SorraTheOrc`) is an **admin** of the `TheWizardsCode` org, so credentials are
  available and creating repos is permitted.
- Remotes use SSH (`git@github.com:...`), consistent with `repo-layout.json`.
- Repos are created once, after F9, in the final `src/` layout.
- **Visibility:** all nine repos are created **public** (producer answer, Q1).
- **Published refs:** push only `dev` plus `main` seeded from it; do **not**
  push the monorepo's feature/`wl-*` branches or its `v0.1.x` tags (Q4).
- **Source revision:** extract from the current `dev` HEAD and record its SHA
  as evidence (producer answer, Q3).

## Existing state

- **F1** delivered `scripts/extract-repos.sh` +
  `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` (history-preserving extraction; verified
  locally: 852 core commits, 23–995 per game).
- **F2** delivered the core-engine repo tree (locally verified standalone).
- **F4** delivered `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` and local per-game checkouts;
  GitHub remote creation was explicitly out of scope (producer gate).
- **F9** reworked per-game repos to repo-root `src/` with alias-only engine
  imports.
- **F5/F7** delivered the launcher distribution and integration verification
  against local sibling checkouts.
- Verified as part of intake: **none** of the nine remotes exist on GitHub
  (`gh api repos/TheWizardsCode/<repo>` → 404).
- The `solo` preset is golf-only; the `full` preset covers all eight games.

## Desired change

Extract all nine repos from the monorepo at the current `dev` HEAD, scaffold the
eight game repos, commit, create the nine GitHub repositories, push each repo's
history to its default branch, and record the per-repo commit counts plus the
source SHA as evidence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/extract-repos.sh` — drives `--target <name>` extraction for the nine
  targets; may need an end-to-end "create remote + push" helper or documented
  commands.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — scaffolds each extracted game checkout.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — source of truth for names/remotes/paths
  (already final; read-only for this task).
- `configs/solo.json`, `configs/full.json` — spot-check sibling composition.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 "GitHub remotes are not created in
  this phase" must be updated to the published state.
- `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — clone-with-submodules instructions.
- `.gitmodules` (per game repo) — `core` submodule wiring.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Visibility / branch model / source revision** — resolved by the producer
  (public; `dev`→`main` with `main` seeded once; current `dev` HEAD with SHA
  recorded); see Appendix Q1–Q3.
- **Published refs** — the filtered clone inherits ~150 branches and 17
  `v0.1.x` tags; publishing only `dev`+`main` avoids stale-branch and cross-repo
  tag confusion (Appendix Q4).
- **History** — preserved as content/provenance, but retained commits receive
  **new SHAs** (inherent to a filtered subset); see Appendix Q3 research.
- `git filter-repo` is not installed on this host — a blocker for real runs
  (fine for `--dry-run`).
- The extraction renames `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` (`--path-rename`) and
  the scaffold rewrites intra-test paths; both history-preserving behaviours were
  verified by F9.
- **Scope-creep risk**: switching the launcher monorepo to point its
  `.gitmodules` at the new remote submodules, adding CI, or publishing npm
  packages are **out of scope**; record any such opportunity as a separate
  child/discovered work item rather than expanding this task.
- Assumption: the agent creates the repos and pushes (this item is the
  authorisation the F4 producer gate deferred).

## Related work

- **F1** *Design architecture & extraction script with history*
  (CG-0MTRO6P18003AZIZ) — the extraction script and repo-layout contract.
- **F2** *Create core-engine repository* (CG-0MTRO6SZH006EBVN) — core tree.
- **F4** *Per-game repos as single-game launchers (local scaffold)*

- **F5** *Launcher distribution with configs/ presets*
  (CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC) — the `solo`/`full` presets used for AC4.
- **F7** *Integration verification — full build & test suite*
  (CG-0MTRO7ECL006ID7J) — local sibling verification precedent.
- **F9** *Per-game repos use src/ source root with alias-based core imports*
  (CG-0MUH0NTRG007GDME) — the final layout this task must publish.
- **Epic** *REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own
  projects* (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17).
- Reference: `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`,
  `docs/dev/per-game-src-layout-decision.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MRPH9YF0008QIZY** – Document TCE game-development best practices as an agent skill (completed)
- **CG-0MOIXHOWP003Y6E0** – Add runtime audio synthesis for dynamic SFX (WebAudio/Tone.js) (completed)
- **CG-0MM03ITUF1SKCSOZ** – Fix Golf browser test failures in CI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, access, added, architecture, avoid (+116 more)
- `AGENTS.md` – matched: acceptance, access, added, architecture, avoid (+102 more)
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — matched: 0muh0ntrg007gdme, architecture, beleaguered, blackjack, build (+96 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (visibility) — ANSWERED.** Should the nine new GitHub repositories be
  **public** or **private**? **Answer (producer):** **public**. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-09-26. Adopt `gh repo create --public` for all nine.
- **Q2 (branch model) — ANSWERED.** Which branch should be the **default** and
  what should be pushed? **Answer (producer):** keep the TCE `dev` → `main`
  flow — seed `main` once from the extracted `dev` history (initial
  publication), then continue dev→main promotion via the ship skill. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-09-26. Options considered: (a) `dev` as default;
  (b) seed `main` once then dev→main; (c) single `main`. Answer = (b).
- **Q3 (source revision) — ANSWERED (condition satisfied).** Extract from the
  current `dev` HEAD (record the SHA), or pin to a stable/tagged commit?
  **Answer (producer):** current `dev` HEAD as recommended, **conditional on
  history being maintained** — the producer asked “will this maintain history?
  Can we maintain history?”.
  - **Research (history preservation):** **Yes.** `git filter-repo` retains
    every commit that touched each repo's selected paths, including author,
    date, message and ancestry, so per-file `git log`/`git blame` continuity is
    preserved; the Option C `example-games/<game>/ → src/` rename is applied in
    the same filter pass, so history follows the file to its new path, and the
    result is pushed verbatim (nothing squashed). Evidence:
    `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §“History preservation”;
    `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (`--path-rename` + `--path` filters); F1’s
    recorded retention counts; local probe `git log -- example-games/golf` =
    103 commits, `git log -- example-games/main-street` = 668 commits; the
    GolfScene.ts `--follow` chain reaches its first commit.
  - **Caveat 1 (SHAs change):** because each repo is a filtered *subset*, the
    retained commits are rewritten and receive **new SHAs** — history content
    and provenance are preserved, hash identity with the monorepo is not.
    (This is inherent to any subset split, including `git subtree`.)
  - **Caveat 2 (what we publish):** the extraction clone inherits the
    monorepo's ~150 branches and 17 `v0.1.x` tags; publish only the intended
    refs (see Q4).
  - **Conclusion:** the condition holds — proceed with current `dev` HEAD and
    record `git rev-parse dev` as evidence. Source: interactive reply,
    2026-09-26.
- **Q4 (published refs) — DECISION RECORDED (producer informed via session
  summary; not re-blocked).** Which refs are pushed to the nine new remotes?
  **Recommended and adopted:** push only the intended long-lived branches —
  `dev` plus `main` seeded from it — and do **not** publish the monorepo's
  feature/`wl-*` branches or its `v0.1.x` release tags (those are engine-wide
  and would be misleading on per-game repos). Tag the new repos from their own
  first release. Rationale: matches the `dev`→`main` model in Q2 and avoids
  150+ stale branches / cross-repo tag confusion. Source: agent recommendation
  recorded 2026-09-26; producer may override.

*(Resolved 2026-09-26. This Appendix is updated idempotently; new open items
would be marked OPEN QUESTION.)*

## Goal

Make every event card's coin/reputation text equal its current integer `card-data.csv` value so the text states the amount the engine actually applies (AC1).

## Context

Producer decision (OPEN QUESTION 1, answer A): `text = data`. 43 events are a plain ×100 rescale; 19 events have pre-existing rebalance drift and must be set to the current data value; 9 percent/duration/no-effect events are unchanged. Data columns must not change (no rebalancing).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every coin/reputation mention in all 71 event `effect` values equals the matching `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` (rule A). Examples: `evt-harvest-festival` → `+600 coins to each Food business and +450 reputation`; `evt-charity-drive` → `+1350 reputation`.
